Hearthline constructed the polynomial from the prior cubic-window program, proved its positive return, priced its ordinary-log reading, and developed the sharp cutoff and fixed integer challenge. paper_scope: The compact positive ruler has variance 1/7 and leaves a positive boundary mass of exactly 1/7 when truncating its signed rows. The elementary all-size quadrature costs O(N log N). The eventual fourteen-copy test on only the primes n^(7/8)<p<=2n is equivalent to ordinary RH. Increasing the fixed power 7/8 gives infinitely many failed heads. Fourteen passes through index 2^36 without gaps. Fifteen pays at every positive index and thirteen fails at every index >=512 on paper. The exact fourteen-copy condition at unbounded indices remains open.
formal_scope: Stock Lean proves positivity of each integer return, divisor regrouping, curvature and leading-cubic bounds, the boundary bracket, the ordinary-log upper price, and the implication from the exact eventual fourteen-copy prime-only comparison to stock RH. The conditional export matches its separately defined integer challenge. Its comparison against bare stock RH rejects the additional premise. The reverse direction, neighboring-count estimates and finite numerical range are paper results.

review.endpoint: The nonnegative limiting height is the stop-loss transform of a probability on [0,1]. All finite truncations integrate to zero. Their gap from the limit is nonnegative, supported through 1/M and has mass exactly 1/7. The integral is evaluated with an actual lower cutoff before the limit.
review.integer_weights: The numerator is a signed sum of ordinary integers. Nonnegativity is proved before converting it to a natural exponent. Above n only the first multiple is present. Each prime exponent in the regrouped ordinary sum was separately recovered by factoring the individual integer labels through physical head 64.
review.forward: No special zero location or PNT is used in the elementary all-size quadrature or forward Lean proof. The formal target preserves the condition n^7<p^8, the exact numerator of every mark, the exponent of the clock, and the eventual quantifier.
review.cutoff: The two omitted disjoint streams are repeated powers and early first powers. The leading cubic of the positive return and partial summation give the exact 1/24 omission cost at the cutoff. Sharpness elsewhere uses the original forward implication and a separately marked RH case, not a counterexample to RH.
review.finite: Direct outward small comparisons, explicit sieve sums through k=512 and overlapping analytic slabs cover every positive index through 2^36. The fractional-moment upper bound is a finite chord interpolation priced with the actual rational ramp. The 21-move estimate prices its entire high-zero tail.
review.independence: The source for the larger finite heads is the earlier independent finite-height estimate. The Alpoge-Claude release and the APCI worktree are not mathematical inputs. No external mathematical review or literature priority determination has been made.
